_readme: Model v2 — the ability-based matcher, run alongside v1 for comparison. This is an OVERLAY on config/profile.json, not a copy: only the fields that define the matching model live here, and everything else — search terms, engagement, skills, penalties, location, ranking defaults — is inherited. That is deliberate. If the two boards differed in their search terms as well as their scoring, a difference between them would not be attributable to the model. Keep it that way: put shared changes in profile.json, and only model-defining changes here.
_capabilitiesComment: THE PRIMARY MATCH AXIS — what she can do, independent of what a job is called. Each entry is an ability evidenced by her résumé, and the phrases are how a posting asks for that ability. This is what lets the board find work under titles she would never have searched for; see README > Matching on ability, not title. Weights are additive with gentle diminishing returns, so a posting wanting six of these outranks one wanting two.

capabilities.label: Finding what is wrong with complex material
capabilities._comment: Her signature ability, and the one with the widest market. 10 years of catching visual, functional and editorial faults before launch.

capabilities.label: Checking work against a written standard
capabilities._comment: The transferable core of QA: not taste, but conformance to a documented rule. Covers brand guidelines, style manuals, accessibility criteria and regulation alike.

capabilities.label: Editorial judgement and clear writing
capabilities._comment: BA English Language & Literature (Honors), plus press releases, brochures and articles at the violin shop, and 'explaining complex ideas clearly' from teaching.

capabilities.label: Systematic testing and sign-off
capabilities._comment: End-to-end QA before deployment: the disciplined, repeatable half of her job.

capabilities.label: Spanish at graduate level
capabilities._comment: MA in Spanish Language & Literature (Honors), doctoral coursework, study abroad in Seville, and three years teaching university Spanish. Far beyond conversational — this is a credential, and localisation QA is the rare role that wants it alongside her QA discipline.

capabilities.label: Teaching, training and curriculum
capabilities._comment: Instructor of Record at WMU — two sections a semester, curriculum aligned to course objectives, technology-integrated lessons. Plus training documentation and in-house classes at Food Dance. This is instructional design experience under a different name.

capabilities.label: Working in a regulated, compliance-sensitive setting
capabilities._comment: Lead Teller at Advia — supervised the teller line while ensuring compliance with federal banking regulations, with accuracy in high-volume transactions. The profile previously ignored this entirely; it is what qualifies her for document review, compliance QA and regulated-content roles.

capabilities.label: Many projects at once, to deadline
Accuracy in data and records
capabilities._comment: High-volume transaction accuracy at the credit union, academic records at WMU, bookkeeping and accounts payable at the violin shop, asset integrity in campaigns.

capabilities.label: Feedback to developers, designers and clients
capabilities._comment: 'Delivered concise, actionable QA feedback… minimizing rework' and deep familiarity with multiple client brands at an agency.

capabilities.label: Customer and member service
capabilities._comment: Credit union teller line, restaurant front-of-house, and customer service for local and national clients — the service instinct behind 'customer-ready'.

_roleFamiliesComment: The career-counsellor layer: role families her résumé supports but that she would not search for by name. `why` is shown on the board so an unfamiliar title arrives with the reason it fits. `queries` feed the keyword searches; `titles` teach the matcher to recognise these names so a family member is not permanently filed as an unknown.

roleFamilies.label: Technical writing & documentation
roleFamilies.why: An English degree, training documentation written from scratch, and ten years of explaining precisely what is wrong to developers and designers. Documentation teams hire exactly this and rarely get it.

roleFamilies.label: Instructional design & training
roleFamilies.why: You were an Instructor of Record: two sections a semester, curriculum built to course objectives, technology-integrated lessons, coursework designed and evaluated. That is instructional design with a different job title on it.

roleFamilies.label: Localization & bilingual quality
roleFamilies.why: A master's in Spanish plus a decade of QA is an unusual pair. Localization QA and translation review want both at once, and most applicants have only one.

roleFamilies.label: Compliance & document review
roleFamilies.why: You supervised a teller line while ensuring compliance with federal banking regulations. Checking documents against rules, at volume, without missing things, is a career of its own — and the QA habit transfers directly.

roleFamilies.label: Digital accessibility
roleFamilies.why: Accessibility auditing is checking digital content against a published written standard and writing up precisely what fails. That is your daily work, with WCAG in place of a brand guide.

roleFamilies.label: Content & knowledge operations
roleFamilies.why: Holding many client brands to their own voice and style, at once, is content governance. The operations side of content is the same job with a wider remit.

roleFamilies.label: Data & catalog quality
roleFamilies.why: Accuracy at volume, whether the volume is banking transactions, academic records, accounts payable, or a product catalog. Data quality teams are hunting for people who actually notice.

roleFamilies.label: Editorial & publishing production
roleFamilies.why: An honors English degree and a production QA habit is what a production editor does — shepherding text through stages without letting an error survive to print.

_titlesComment: v2 moves some title groups into roleFamilies so they are presented as new directions with a rationale rather than as business as usual. Expressed as edits to v1's groups rather than a replacement list, so search terms added to v1 keep working here.
_rankingComment: Controls the 'new directions' feature — roles outside her current title. A posting whose title names a roleFamily always qualifies. A posting with no recognisable title must instead evidence discoveryMinCapabilities distinct abilities, which is what keeps keyword coincidences out. discoveryFloor lifts these clear of the 'possible' band so they are actually seen; incumbentTitleWeight is how core an existing title must be to outrank a new-direction label, and roleFamilyTitleWeight is what a family title is worth on its own.
